title: FeBiM: Efficient and Compact Bayesian Inference Engine Empowered with Ferroelectric In-Memory Computing
problem: Existing in-memory computing architectures optimize for neural network MAC operations and cannot efficiently implement Bayesian inference, which requires cumulative probability multiplications. This incompatibility prevents deployment of interpretable Bayesian models on efficient hardware.
motivation: Bayesian inference provides superior interpretability and uncertainty estimation for scenarios with limited data, but lacks efficient hardware implementations.
method: FeBiM uses multi-bit ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) in a crossbar array to encode Bayesian model probabilities. Quantized logarithmic probabilities map to discrete FeFET states, and accumulated crossbar outputs naturally compute posterior probabilities without additional calculation circuitry, leveraging the additive properties of logarithmic probability multiplication.
key_novelty: FeBiM is the first FeFET-based in-memory computing engine specifically designed for Bayesian inference, mapping logarithmic probabilities directly to ferroelectric device states for native posterior computation.
contributions: First FeFET-based in-memory Bayesian inference engine
Novel quantized logarithmic probability encoding scheme mapping to discrete ferroelectric states
Achieves 26.32 Mb/mm² storage density (10.7× improvement in compactness)
Achieves 581.40 TOPS/W computing efficiency (43.4× improvement over state-of-the-art)
